\\u0060TaskAggregate.AssignedOwnerFingerprint\\u0060/\\u0060TaskDetails.AssignedOwnerFingerprint\\u0060/\\u0060TaskListItem.AssignedOwnerFingerprint\\u0060; \\u0060TaskDecider.GrantTake\\u0060 populates it from the aggregate\\u0027s own already-verified \\u0060PendingTakeRequestedByOwnerFingerprint\\u0060; \\u0060DispatchEngine.IsGrantedToThisOwner\\u0060 (internal static, pure) is the new claim-gate decision, used in both \\u0060TryClaimAsync\\u0060 and the widened \\u0060ReadQueueAsync\\u0060 filter; \\u0060h9k task show\\u0060\\u0027s \\u0060AssigneeMarkupAsync\\u0060 does a fingerprint-first resolution with a reverse-lookup fallback.\\n- Non-obvious shape: \\u0060TaskAggregate.Apply\\u0060 is a pure, I/O-free fold and cannot look up local \\u0060OwnerDetails\\u0060, so \\u0060AssignedOwnerId\\u0060 still reflects whatever Guid the event self-declares even on a forged grant \\u2014 the actual security boundary is the fingerprint comparison at the two places that hold a document session (the daemon\\u0027s claim gate, \\u0060h9k task show\\u0060), not inside the aggregate. If a future reviewer expects \\u0060AssignedOwnerId\\u0060 itself to come back null on a forged grant, that\\u0027s the reason it doesn\\u0027t; the fingerprint field is what carries the real signal.\\n- Deliberately left undone: fingerprint verification wasn\\u0027t extended to \\u0060TaskWorkCommand\\u0060/\\u0060TaskStartCommand\\u0060/\\u0060TaskDelegateCommand\\u0060\\u0027s human-facing ownership checks or to the background sweep filters in \\u0060JiraWriteRetryEngine\\u0060/\\u0060RemoteStackedParentSweep\\u0060/\\u0060CloseoutEngine\\u0060, all of which still compare \\u0060AssignedOwnerId\\u0060 by Guid alone. This is a conscious scope call (the task\\u0027s own boundary note and acceptance criteria both name the dispatch claim gate specifically), not an oversight \\u2014 worth a follow-up task if that residual matters in practice.
